case: domain-over-enum COALESCE parameter inference in both argument positions
outcome: Exact native PostgreSQL behavior: the text/NULL parameter and COALESCE result use the base enum type, while the source column remains the declared domain type.
contract: COALESCE(status, $1) and COALESCE($1, status) infer text and SQL NULL parameters as the target enum.
Text and NULL cases preserve the exact expected values for rows containing ready, paused and SQL NULL.
pg_typeof verifies the parameter and expression use the base enum while pg_typeof(status) remains the outer domain.
The adjacent domain-over-enum contract group, including this new case, passes.
initial_observation: The first test expectation assumed the COALESCE result would retain the domain. PostgreSQL instead resolves the expression and parameter to the base enum; the corrected test records this native type-resolution behavior and separately asserts the source column remains a domain.
remaining: Other direct query contexts, enum/session configurations and the wider B3 matrix remain open; this case does not qualify 0.2.0.
